y-m-30-05.goal: Use the property that opposite angles in cyclic quadrilateral add to 180° to check claim “rhombus always cyclic”; make different sets of 4 angles meeting constraints.
y-m-30-05.material: Quadrilateral with all 4 vertices on a circle called “cyclic quadrilateral”. For cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angle sizes sum to 180°. Jiho think, “Rhombus, with 4 equal sides, always cyclic.” (Rhombus opposite angles equal.)

y-m-30-05.s.s1.explain: In rhombus ∠C=∠A=70°, so ∠A+∠C=140°≠180°. If cyclic, opposite pair must total 180°, but no. This rhombus no cyclic.

y-m-30-05.s.s2.fail.c1: All four angles must be integers greater than 0 degrees.

y-m-30-05.s.s2.fail.c4: If ∠A=∠C, it might be parallelogram. Make dem different.
y-m-30-05.s.s2.explain: If both ∠A+∠C and ∠B+∠D equal 180°, total automatically 360°. If ∠A≠∠C, no parallelogram. Examples: (70°,80°,110°,100°) and (60°,90°,120°,90°).

y-m-30-05.s.s3.model.1: Only rhombus with all right angles—a square—possible. Opposite rhombus angles equal, so 2x=180°, x=90°.

y-m-30-08.title: Longest stick that fit inside box
y-m-30-08.topic: Diagonal of rectangular box (Pythagorean theorem in 3D)
y-m-30-08.goal: Find segment length in solid using base diagonal and height perpendicular; make different boxes with natural-number diagonal; judge if stick fits.
y-m-30-08.material: Empty rectangular box 3cm wide, 4cm deep, 12cm high. Put very thin straight stick fully inside. Ignore box thickness; inner measurements same as outer. Find longest stick that fit.
y-m-30-08.thinking.0: Find wrong line in solution with error
y-m-30-08.thinking.2: Judge by comparing result with stick length
y-m-30-08.prereq.1: Position of edges and faces of box (base perpendicular to height)
y-m-30-08.s.s1.prompt: Below is one student's solution to find longest stick length. Choose wrong line. Count from 1.
y-m-30-08.s.s1.hint.0: Explain in words how stick goes from one box edge to opposite top edge; look at angle between 5 and 12 in line 3.
y-m-30-08.s.s1.hint.1: Draw triangle made from 5cm, 12cm, and stick. Use triangle side relationship to see if lengths 5,12,17 possible. [12 5]
y-m-30-08.s.s1.line.2: Stick lies in shape connecting base diagonal 5 and height 12, so 5+12=17.
y-m-30-08.s.s1.explain: Line 3 wrong. Stick cross from one base corner to opposite top corner, so base diagonal 5 and height 12 perpendicular, and stick hypotenuse of right triangle whose legs are those two. Hypotenuse no be sum; e be square root of sum of squares, so shorter. Thus 17cm in line 4 wrong too. Correct: √(5²+12²)=13cm.
y-m-30-08.s.s2.prompt: Among box widths a, depths b, heights c all natural from 1 to 12, make 3 different boxes where longest stick length also natural. (a,b,c) in different order count same.
y-m-30-08.s.s2.hint.0: Choose 2 lengths, find base diagonal squared; change height and check if total becomes square.
y-m-30-08.s.s2.hint.1: Compare your boxes with original 3,4,12; try in order from small values same way. [3 4]

y-m-30-08.s.s2.explain: For example (1,2,2) gives √9=3; (2,3,6) gives √49=7; (4,4,7) gives √81=9; (2,4,4) gives √36=6. Original (3,4,12) gives √169=13, so it also meet condition. [1 2 2 2 3 3 4 4 4 4]
